messages:
soren: Heads-up: after yesterday's kernel-selector patch (optimize-for-latency) we're seeing p95 host overhead for short requests up ~25ms. GPU profiles look fine.

soren: Quick numbers from the trace sampler (short chat workload):
```
host_total_ms p50: 2.1  p95: 68 (+25)  p99: 95
parse+tokenize_ms p50: 0.6 p95: 18 (+16)
stream_chunking_ms p95: 4.2 (extra small writes)
kvcache_lookup_ms p95: 1.0
```

chi: The patch added a "lookahead kernel-fingerprint" that peeks at token boundaries to pick kernels/quant paths earlier. That lookahead runs inside the ingress hot path.

emily: Can you share a flamegraph? If lookahead forces proto_unwrap/utf8_norm it could be the culprit (those touch ICU and memcpy).

soren: Flamegraph attached (summarized): heavy stack under ingress.read_frame -> lookahead_peek -> proto_unwrap -> utf8_normalize -> token_split -> call_token_adapter_old. Also a separate hotspot in streaming: many small writev syscall nodes.

emily: Streaming chunker change also landed in same window? I remember a tweak to align chunk sizes to 256 bytes to match a kernel batch heuristic. That can make many tiny frames for short payloads. Which commits are in the blamelist?

soren: Blamelist: 7b2a9d (kernel-selector lookahead) -> 3c9f1a (chunk-align-256) -> 5a4f00 (minor mapping fix).

niko: Two problems then: (1) lookahead triggers legacy token adapter for some header shapes; (2) chunk-align causes extra small frames breaking writev coalescing.

chi: Exactly. The fingerprint map has a fallback that classifies some grpc header variants as "legacy" when only 1st 32 bytes are inspected. Lookahead uses 64 bytes and hits that rule more often.

emily: Repro steps I used: send 3-5 token prompt over grpc streaming with small metadata -> observe p95 delta. Strace showed extra open("/usr/lib/icu/...") on the slow runs (ICU load), and many writev(2..5) calls per request instead of single batched writev.

infra-bot: Canary rollback: reverted 7b2a9d on canary at 09:12 UTC.

soren: After rollback the p95 dropped back within 8 minutes. KV hit rates unchanged, so not a kvcache regression. This is definitely host-side parse/tokenization + streaming framing overhead.

niko: Proposed remediation plan:
- disable lookahead kernel-fingerprint on ingress hot path (use async fingerprinting outside critical path)
- fix fingerprint mapping to include grpc-framing shapes so token_adapter_v2 is chosen for common short-chat headers
- revert chunk-align-256 or change it to prefer coalesced writes (only align if payload > threshold)
- add a small-request e2e perf test exercising grpc streaming and short prompts

chi: Also add an ascii-fastpath for tokenization: quick byte scan to avoid ICU when bytes are all 1-byte ASCII; cheap and covers a lot of short prompts. Put it before any heavy normalization during lookahead.

emily: I'll open a draft PR that disables lookahead and adds the ascii-fastpath tests. Niko can work on chunker coalescing fallback.

soren: Marking P1 for Hosted and P0 for Dedicated (we're seeing customer impact on pinned capacity). Blamelist noted.

infra-bot: Deploy pipeline: running stateless-canary with lookahead disabled and chunker coalesce heuristic at 10:40 UTC. Will collect traces for 30m.

niko: FYI, I also saw similar small-write fanout on HTTP/2 edge when using ALPN negotiator + writev split. I'll sync with edge-team on a coalescing knob.

chi: Good catch. Let's keep tracking: if stateless canary trace shows p95 -> baseline we merge changes; otherwise we'll iterate.

soren: Thanks all, please paste any traces in this thread.
